intro: You've searched for an ACCA accountant near me, which usually means you want a qualified accountant you can actually meet or speak to locally. ACCA members are chartered certified accountants, so the letters after their name tell you they've passed a demanding qualification and follow a professional ethics code. Here's what to check and what to tell us so we can introduce you to a suitable accountant near you.
need_heading: What people searching for an ACCA accountant nearby usually need
need_lead: Most people want a qualified accountant they can reach easily, who understands their situation and can quote for the work.
needs: You run a small business or work as a sole trader and want an accountant who can handle your tax and accounts without a long journey.
You've recently moved to the area and need someone local to take over your bookkeeping, payroll or self assessment.
You want to check that the person you're dealing with is genuinely an ACCA member and not just using the word accountant.
You're starting a new venture and want a face-to-face chat about what records to keep and how to stay on the right side of HMRC.
You've had a bad experience with a remote accountant and would prefer someone you can sit down with when something important comes up.
context_heading: What the letters ACCA actually mean
context: In the UK, the word accountant on its own isn't a protected title, so anyone can use it. ACCA members are different: they're chartered certified accountants who have passed a demanding qualification, follow ACCA's ethics code and complete continuing professional development. You can check whether someone is a member through the ACCA register.

If a firm offers public practice services, it also needs an ACCA practising certificate, and every accountancy practice must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes by a professional body or HMRC. It's reasonable to ask which body supervises the firm, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance, and how complaints are handled. Only registered auditors can sign statutory audit reports.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: The area or town you'd like the accountant to be near, and how far you're willing to travel.
Whether you're an individual, a sole trader, a partnership or a limited company, so we can match the right kind of practice.
The main work you need help with, such as annual accounts, tax returns, payroll, VAT or bookkeeping.
Whether you'd prefer to meet in person or are happy with phone and email contact.
Any deadlines or particular concerns, such as a letter from HMRC or a change in your business.
That you specifically want an ACCA-qualified accountant, so we can take that into account when introducing you.
questions: Are you a member of ACCA, and can you show me your practising certificate if you offer public practice services?
Which body supervises your firm for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How do you handle complaints if something goes wrong?
What experience do you have with clients in my situation?
How will you charge for the work, and what will you need from me to give a quote?

faqs.q: How can I check that an accountant is really ACCA-qualified?
faqs.a: You can search the ACCA register online or ask the accountant for their membership number. A genuine member will be happy to point you to the register. If a firm offers public practice services, you can also ask to see their ACCA practising certificate.

faqs.q: Does an ACCA accountant have to be local to me?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but many people prefer someone nearby for face-to-face meetings. If you search for an ACCA accountant near me, you're probably looking for that convenience. It's fine to ask how they usually work with clients and whether they visit your area.

faqs.q: What's the difference between an ACCA accountant and a chartered accountant?
faqs.a: Both are protected titles with demanding qualifications and professional ethics codes. ACCA members are chartered certified accountants, while chartered accountants may belong to ICAEW, ICAS or Chartered Accountants Ireland. The right choice depends on your needs, so ask about their experience with clients like you.

faqs.q: Will an ACCA accountant handle my tax return or payroll?
faqs.a: Many ACCA practices offer a wide range of services, from tax returns to payroll and bookkeeping. ACCA members can work with sole traders through to large companies. It's best to ask directly whether they cover the specific work you need.
